item.title: Present perfect: ever, never and experiences
item.explanation_text: Use have or has + past participle to talk about experiences in your life up to now, when the exact time is not important: I have visited Bukhara. She has never eaten sushi. Ask with ever: Have you ever flown on a plane? Short answers: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. Regular past participles end in -ed (visited, worked). Many common verbs are irregular: be → been, see → seen, eat → eaten, ride → ridden, do → done. Use been (not gone) for a place you visited and came back from. If you say when it happened (yesterday, in 2022, last summer), use the past simple: I visited Bukhara last summer.
item.contrast_text: Compare: I have been to Samarkand (some time in my life). I went to Samarkand last summer (a finished time).
item.common_error_pattern: Using the past simple form after have ('I have saw'), or using the present perfect with a finished time ('I have seen him yesterday').

examples.bad: I have seen that film last week.
examples.good: I saw that film last week.
